idea-plugin.name: Vernac
idea-plugin.description:
Domain-Driven Design for Java, expressed in Vernac.

Vernac is a domain-specific language for defining typed identifiers, value objects, entities, aggregates, events, repositories, ports, services, and use cases. Its compiler generates Java code following consistent architectural conventions, while custom business logic remains Java.

Create your first project

Select New Project → Vernac to create a Maven project with a small domain model and a Java test. Choose your project name, Maven coordinates, Java package, and a registered JDK with Java 21 or newer.

  • Ready-to-build project template with Maven Wrapper
  • Consistent package declarations, imports, and source paths
  • Automatic Maven import
  • Automatic opening of the initial Vernac model
  • Project-specific README with build instructions

Editor features

  • Automatic recognition of .vernac files
  • Semantic highlighting
  • Debug embedded Java in Vernac source: breakpoints, stepping, variables, expression evaluation and completion, conditions and logpoints (0.5.0 development).
  • Syntax and semantic diagnostics
  • Code completion and snippets
  • Hover documentation
  • Go to Declaration for definitions within Vernac
  • New Namespace creates the Vernac directory structure
  • New Vernac File derives its namespace automatically from the selected directory

Language server and code generation

Open a .vernac file to activate language support. The language server is bundled and starts automatically. No separate language server installation or LSP4IJ configuration is required.

Java source generation runs through the Vernac Maven plugin. Projects created by the wizard already include its configuration. For existing projects, add the Maven plugin to your build.

Vernac build dependencies

Projects created by this plugin use Vernac @project.version@. Published release artifacts are downloaded automatically from Maven Central.

If the version ends in -SNAPSHOT, install the matching Vernac artifacts in your local Maven repository before building the generated project. Follow the Vernac repository build instructions.

The bundled language server provides editor support; Maven resolves the compiler and runtime dependencies separately.

The starter example requires no database, Docker, or running Spring application. Internet access is needed for the initial download of Maven and dependencies.

Project status

Vernac is under active development. Language syntax and generated APIs may change between releases.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Live services, events, ports and usecase APIs

Embedded Java can resolve current local service operations, event factories, port contracts and usecase APIs before generation, including self dependency views and nested Result records. Uses the same generators as the compiler.

Live entities, aggregates and behavior access views

Entity/aggregate factories, field getters and public behaviors are now visible before Java generation, together with Read/Write/Access views for the appropriate self context. Entity and aggregate collections expose their existing typed id helpers. The actual model class gains no public setters. Invalid owners withhold their complete API family, and stale owned access views are suppressed. Installed-IDE acceptance is pending.

Live IDs, enums and value-side collections before generation

New local IDs, enum values and explicit list/set types now use the same generator-backed Java views as ordinary value objects: factories, enum constants, typed collection methods and public behaviors. Multiple collections retain independent APIs. Invalid declarations are withheld; current unsaved types are visible without running Maven. Enum constants navigate to their model declaration. The mutable-domain expansion above also covers entity/aggregate collections. Ordinary-VO completion is confirmed in the IDE; the new type kinds await acceptance.

Live VO completion across temporary editor copies

New ordinary VO names now insert without technical package prefixes (confirmed in the IDE). Copied Vernac hosts retain their original model scope, and existing domain packages are wrapped before the first editor snapshot. This targets missing factory-member completion such as EditorTest.o; this path is now confirmed in the installed IDE.

Scoped Java package lookup for live VO imports and factories

Java package lookup now retains current VO APIs, including during native completion's alternative-resolve mode. Stable source provenance preserves class identity across snapshot recreation during insertion. Visible Vernac types already have projected imports; no technical package name or new Java import is required in the source. Diagnostics include imports, package lookups, factory signatures, the caret reference and copied-host provenance.

Inspect embedded Java resolution

Tools → Vernac → Diagnose Embedded Java Context opens an in-memory report of live domain publication, injection, scopes and Java lookup at the caret. It does not modify or upload project files. This diagnoses the reported live-completion failure; it is not a completion fix.

Keep live VO APIs visible through injected Java scope unions

Recognizes the live host context inside IntelliJ's combined host/injected-file search scope, restoring the bridge used by Java resolution and class-name lookup. Ambiguous combined host contexts are rejected. Diagnostic reports now show union branches and inspect short-name extensions in the correct project area. Installed-IDE retest pending.

Live Java APIs for new value objects

Embedded Java can resolve ordinary value-object factories, getters, public behaviors and validation Read views from the current model before generation. Java views stay in memory; owned older VO sources are replaced in Vernac Java scopes only. This first slice does not provide live APIs for IDs, enums, collections, aggregates or usecase access interfaces.

Keep valid declarations while editing incomplete files

Editor analysis now retains complete declarations when another declaration in the same file is malformed. Valid Java contexts and declaration navigation remain available; syntax errors are still reported and builds remain strict. This is groundwork for completion before generation.

Generated Java in embedded code

Recognizes the conventional generated Java source root after Maven generation, so embedded Java can resolve generated domain classes, factories and inferred local types without a manual Maven reload. Sources still need an initial generation build.

0.5.0 development — Consistent Java implementation contracts

Optional arguments are nullable throughout inline/external implementations and helpers; Optional getters and results retain their contract. Short implemented-by names resolve through local Java imports or the generated caller package, including native class navigation. Shared Java signature checks report overload collisions early. Missing required public domain arguments consistently raise domain validation errors.

The Spring Boot starter now runs directly from its application class: no profile selection is needed for local development. The wizard also delegates IDE builds and runs to Maven, so Vernac sources are generated before Java compilation. Explicit deployment profiles replace the local default; the supplied Dockerfile selects production.

0.5.0 development — Declare server-rendered pages

Inbound MVC adapters connect HTML views and URL-encoded forms to typed usecases. Declare rendering, local redirects, safe error pages and form redisplay in Vernac; generated controllers preserve permitted inputs, exclude sensitive fields and never retry a failed POST. Completion, diagnostics, page-loader navigation and hover are integrated. The Spring Boot starter now uses this MVC boundary instead of handwritten controller/error glue; Thymeleaf templates and security remain application-owned.

0.5.0 development — Start with a real application

New Project can create a complete, compact Spring Boot application: a responsive Thymeleaf task workspace, PostgreSQL, generated transactional usecases and JDBC repositories, local Docker Compose, matching Flyway migration/history, CSRF-protected forms, domain/web tests and environment-based deployment configuration. The web application is the wizard default; minimal domain projects and reusable type modules remain available.

0.5.0 development — Native type navigation

Declared Vernac type usages now expose precise PSI references for IntelliJ's Ctrl-hover link feedback and navigation, including matching vocabulary term names. Approved Java types in DSL signatures and explicit implemented-by classes link to their actual Java declarations. Java navigation and helper resolution stay available in files containing terms. Namespace/import/module visibility follows the compiler; embedded Java retains native Java references. Cross-language rename remains separate work.

0.5.0 development — Debug your application in Vernac

Set breakpoints directly in your Vernac source, step through embedded Java, inspect arguments and local variables, and use Evaluate Expression, completion, conditional breakpoints and logpoints with the mapped Java scope.

  • Domain behaviors, usecases, domain services and listener execute bodies, including their private helpers.
  • Inline outbound adapter behavior, inbound/outbound Java mappings, declarative field conversions and inbound execute argument assignments.
  • Require-rule breakpoints on value objects, entities, aggregates, usecases, domain services and event payloads.
  • Read/Access and validation-input facades show stored readable properties while preserving their real types. Optional backing values are labeled explicitly; projected children add no write access. Display never invokes behavior methods.
  • Conservative stepping skips verified pure facade reads; modification guards, validators and real call stacks remain intact. Contributor mode restores raw views.
  • Source/build/runtime checks prevent stale generated classes from being presented as current Vernac source. Contributors can switch to generated Java views.

The core debugger workflow and adapter/mapping paths have been exercised in IntelliJ. Facade presentation/filtering has real-JVM inspection tests and a guided UI acceptance check. See the Debugging tutorial. Use matching 0.5.0 development compiler and plugin builds.

Domain diagram export uses the supported blocking read-action API for its short document snapshot on the UI thread.

Vernac 0.4.0

Versioned modules, pagination, inbound error policies, ubiquitous language and domain diagrams.

See the architecture

Tools → Vernac → Show Domain Diagram exports the current namespace and opens a Mermaid Markdown view with domain vocabulary. PlantUML and JSON exports accompany it. The action includes unsaved Vernac documents and uses the built dependency index.

Ubiquitous language beside the model

  • Define namespaced terms, including quoted concepts with spaces, with descriptions, examples and notes.
  • Type hover displays exact-name vocabulary, including documentation from exported module types without source attachments.
  • Term navigation, entry completion and highlighting share compiler semantics.
  • Maven compilation produces readable and machine-readable glossaries; generated Java source carries associated JavaDoc.

Versioned modules: complete 0.4.0 scope

  • Publish explicit contracts and reuse compiled implementations from Maven dependencies.
  • Activate usecases, services, repositories, listeners and HTTP entrypoints; select outbound providers through fixed or profile-dependent bindings.
  • Coordinate independent module/application histories and durable event delivery.
  • Navigate activation identities to read-only module overviews, including modules without exports.
  • Refresh dependency symbols after rebuilt indexes; show incompatible-module diagnostics on open composition files.
  • Preserve source navigation for events and multiple collections in dependency contract views.

Metadata uses module-contracts-9. Rebuild producers and consumers after updating development tools. Updated contracts, language/AI references, FAQs, project guidance and lifecycle examples describe the supported scope.

Declarative inbound error policies

Added ordered endpoint and adapter error rules with typed rejection codes, integration responsibility/category selectors and safe public replies. Diagnostics, enum navigation, category completion and highlighting share the compiler contract.

Multiple domain collections

Declare several lists and sets per ID, value, enum, entity or aggregate. Each collection has an independent optional name and behavior. Completion, declaration navigation and embedded-Java receivers include every collection.

Paginated usecase results and HTTP

Added explicit offset, counted offset and cursor value-list results, independent Result components and page DTO fields. ACL maps entries while retaining metadata; GET responses contain completed pages. Updated completion/navigation and added safe INVALID_CURSOR error handling. Dispatch now includes a paged board API.

Cursor repository pagination

Added find cursor with ordered aggregate lists, deletion-independent continuation, mixed sort directions and query/filter/schema-bound encrypted cursors. Added cursor completion/highlighting and shared key configuration.

Offset repository pagination

Added find offset queries with optional counting, ordered aggregate lists, typed page/traversal APIs, configurable page-size limits and snapshot-consistent root counts. Added completion and semantic highlighting for offset/counting.

Pagination runtime foundation

Typed requests, completed offset/counted/cursor pages and sequential lazy traversal are available in the runtime. Repository offset/cursor queries and materialized usecase/HTTP page results are supported.

Typed adapter configuration: diagnostics, configuration-type completion, and navigation from a REST base to its configuration declaration.

Generated API readability

Access interfaces now use domain.access. Go to Declaration on technical interface types keeps standard Java navigation. Validation injection no longer adds an artificial negation.

Entity and aggregate contracts

Added domain-field and containment-cycle diagnostics, including optional fields and collections across namespaces. Aggregate metadata is isolated from write behavior.

Validation delegates

Java support inside validates expressions now uses a read-only self interface, including Optional getters, read behavior, and shared Java imports.

Entity and aggregate behavior

  • Added read/modify behavior with Read, Write, and Access contracts.
  • Injected Java uses the matching self interface for completion and analysis.
  • Java navigation now includes entity and aggregate contracts and behavior.

Java to Vernac member navigation

  • Generated VO getters navigate to their field declarations; ID value() navigates to the ID declaration.
  • Public inline and implemented-by behavior methods navigate to their Vernac contracts.
  • Overloads use exact resolved parameter types; ambiguous or stale signatures keep normal Java navigation.

Java to Vernac type navigation

  • Go to Declaration on generated ID, value-object, enum and collection type references now opens the Vernac definition.
  • Uses compiler ownership metadata and exact type identities; ordinary Java classes keep normal navigation.
  • Reads current model content, including unsaved changes, in the referenced type's Maven module.

Inline Java behavior — first integration

  • Added Java language injection for inline behavior method bodies.
  • Private helpers share a Java context; method declarations retain Vernac source positions.
  • Uses the compiler's namespace/import rules and includes unsaved model changes.
  • Generate the domain Java sources first for receiver and model API resolution.

Project-wide type assistance

  • Type and import completion use namespace visibility across Vernac files.
  • Go to Declaration follows resolved type references and explicit imports.
  • Unsaved edits are included; ambiguous names have no arbitrary navigation target.
  • Grouped namespace/file actions near the top of New and hid duplicate generic template entries.

Namespace creation

  • Added New → Vernac Namespace with namespace-name validation.
  • New → Vernac File now derives the namespace from its target directory.
  • Updated file templates to the namespace syntax and an ID/VO example.

0.1.0-dev.3 — Project creation

  • Added the New Project → Vernac wizard.
  • Added editable Maven coordinates and Java package.
  • Added selection of registered JDKs with Java 21 or newer.
  • Included a Maven Wrapper, sample domain model, and Java test.
  • Added automatic Maven import and initial model opening.
  • Added a project-specific README.
  • Added template preflight checks and project generation tests.

Earlier development versions — Editor integration

  • Registered the Vernac language and file type.
  • Bundled the language server with automatic startup.
  • Connected editor features through the IntelliJ LSP API.
  • Added Vernac file templates.
